questions.title: How does the non‑uniformity in RoPE dimensions affect positional interpolation?
questions.question_body: In Section 3.2 the paper states that lower RoPE dimensions (higher frequency) require less interpolation while higher dimensions (low frequency) can be interpolated more. Could someone explain the intuition behind this dimensional non‑uniformity and how it improves the model’s positional encoding for very long sequences?

questions.title: What is the role of the token‑position threshold τ̂ in Equation (2)?
questions.question_body: Equation (2) introduces a threshold τ̂ that determines whether the rescale factor λ_i is applied to a token’s position. I’m not clear why the first τ̂ tokens are kept un‑scaled and how this choice interacts with the attention distribution in Transformers. How does this influence the performance at different sequence lengths?

questions.title: Why does the evolutionary search impose a monotonic constraint on λ_i across RoPE dimensions?
questions.question_body: The search algorithm restricts λ_i to satisfy λ_i ≤ λ_{i+1}. Is this purely based on the NTK theory, or are there empirical observations that justify this monotonicity? What would happen if we allowed non‑monotonic λ_i values?

questions.title: How is the ‘effective rescale factor’ computed in practice for a given extension ratio s?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions that λ_i can be up to s × 1.25 with a 0.01 step size. When extending from 4k to 128k (s = 32), does that mean λ_i ranges from 1.0 to 40.0? How does the algorithm handle such large search ranges without exploding the search space?

questions.title: Can you clarify the difference between Pi, NTK, and YaRN interpolation strategies?
questions.question_body: Section 3.1 describes Pi as linear scaling, NTK as frequency‑aware scaling, and YaRN as a hybrid that groups dimensions. I’m confused about how each strategy mathematically transforms the original RoPE angles and why YaRN performs worse on PG19 data compared to Pi.

questions.title: What is the intuition behind the two‑step progressive extension strategy?
questions.question_body: The authors first fine‑tune a model to 256k and then run a second interpolation search to reach 2048k. Why is fine‑tuning directly to 2048k infeasible, and how does the intermediate 256k fine‑tuning help the second search step?

questions.title: How does LongRoPE recover performance on shorter contexts after extreme extension?
questions.question_body: After extending to a 512× window, the paper mentions a performance drop on the original 4k context. The authors mitigate this by running an extra search for short lengths. Could someone explain the mechanism of this recovery and how the new rescale factors are applied at inference time?

questions.title: Why are the rescale factors allowed to exceed the extension ratio s in the search space?
questions.question_body: The search space allows λ_i to go up to s × 1.25, which means more interpolation than simple linear scaling. How does increasing λ_i beyond the naive interpolation ratio help preserve positional information, and under what circumstances does this happen?

questions.title: What are the practical GPU and memory requirements for a 2088k-long RoPE search?
questions.question_body: The paper claims the search is efficient, but for a target context length of 2M tokens, what kind of hardware is needed? How many GPU hours does a typical search take, and what percentage of it is dominated by perplexity evaluation versus genetic operations?

questions.title: How does the Cosine/Sine encoding formula in Equation (1) change after applying the searched rescale factors?
questions.question_body: Equation (1) shows the standard RoPE formulation. After the search, each dimension gets its own λ_i and a token‑position threshold. Can someone write out the modified formula explicitly for a token at position n and dimension i to see the exact scaling applied?

questions.title: Why does increasing the starting token threshold τ̂ help at very long extensions but not at 2048k?
questions.question_body: The ablation study indicates that keeping the first tokens uninterpolated benefits performance at 16k and 32k but becomes less effective at 2048k. What is the theoretical explanation for this diminishing return as the extension ratio grows?
